reasons: Government (ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ) land WITHOUT Saguvali Chit — severe title risk

major_risks: Owner category classified as 'Government/ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ' without any Saguvali Chit (grant certificate) mentioned, indicating the land may still vest with the Government
Absence of Saguvali Chit raises serious doubt on the private alienability of the land
Acquisition shown as 'RR-829 ಪಿತ್ರಾಜಿತ' (ancestral) which conflicts with Government owner category — ambiguity in title
District field is blank in RTC — incomplete record
positive_findings: Named individual cultivator/occupant (ಕುಳ್ಳೇಗೌಡ ಬಿನ್ ಚನ್ನ) is recorded with long continuous possession period (since 28-11-2001)
reasoning: Per the guideline matrix, 'Government' owner category without a Saguvali Chit is a HIGH risk indicator (70+).
Without a Saguvali/Grant Certificate, the occupant has no transferable title; any sale could be void and attract resumption by the Government.
The contradictory acquisition type ('ಪಿತ್ರಾಜಿತ' — ancestral) alongside Government ownership suggests either an unresolved grant, encroachment entry, or a Darkhast case that is not yet regularised.
Although there is no court stay, mutation or PTCL flag — which otherwise would push risk higher — the fundamental title defect (Government land, no grant) itself keeps the score in the HIGH band.
Blank district and the small holding size (25 guntas) further reduce verifiability.
recommendations: Obtain and verify the Saguvali Chit / Grant Certificate; if unavailable, treat the land as non-transferable Government land.
Procure Mutation Register (MR) extracts and the full Index of Lands to trace how occupancy was recorded.
Check for any Darkhast grant order, conditions of grant, and non-alienation period from the Tahsildar's office.
Verify PTCL applicability independently from the Assistant Commissioner, as RTC entries can miss SC/ST grant history.
Obtain Form 10 (RR Register), Akarband, Tippani, and Village Map to confirm identity and extent.
Insist on 30-year Encumbrance Certificate (Form 15) and family tree certificate from the Revenue authorities.
Do NOT proceed with any advance/token payment until Government ownership classification is resolved through a Khatha regularisation or confirmed Saguvali grant.
llm_risk.summary: The RTC reflects Government ownership category without any Saguvali Chit, which is a fundamental title defect making the land presumptively non-transferable despite the occupant's long possession. While there are no court stays, restrictions, PTCL flags, or pending mutations, the Government classification alone warrants a HIGH risk rating. Buyer should not proceed until grant/regularisation documents are produced and verified.
